name: ctx_delta.v1
description: The ctx.delta data-channel payload (docs/07 §6, docs/13 §4): changed components only, base_seq-verified merge onto the last snapshot or delta. This is the one ctx.* payload shape with no existing authority elsewhere in protocol/ — data_channel_envelope.v1.json's 'ctx_delta_payload' $def deliberately stays generic ('Component shape authority is docs/07 / screen_context.v1.json') and this file is that authority for the delta-specific parts. It is deliberately NOT the same file as screen_context.v1.json even though 'changed' entries look like components: duplicating the full sixteen-role oneOf here would create two copies of that discriminated union that could silently drift apart, which is precisely the coherence risk a protocol freeze exists to prevent. Instead 'changed'/'removed' entries are validated at the identity+common-fields level (role from the same closed vocabulary, plus the fields any role can carry) — a consumer that needs full per-role shape validation on the merged result validates the post-merge state against screen_context.v1.json instead, which is exactly what SnapshotIngestor's merge-then-store flow does (docs/08 §4.1: deltas merge into ctx:{session_id}, read back as the full IR). additionalProperties is left unset throughout, matching the rest of this protocol family's additive-within-v1 posture (docs/13 §9).

base_seq.description: seq of the last snapshot or delta this delta merges onto — NOT simply the previous message's seq, because ctx.event shares the single client seq counter without advancing screen state (docs/13 §4). SnapshotIngestor rejects a merge whose base_seq does not match the state actually held (docs/08 §4.1).

changed.description: Components whose serialized form changed since the base state, each carried in full (docs/07 §6) — not a field-level diff of the previous value.

removed.description: Components no longer present, by identity. Wire identity is role+label (docs/07 §6: 'Component identity for diffing is testTag when present, else role + label') — testTag itself never appears on the wire in any fixture in this protocol, so the wire-level identity used for removal is always role+label; a component whose label changed fails identity matching and appears as a remove+add pair, which is accepted per docs/07 §6.

last_action.description: Present only when the action that produced this delta changed (docs/07 §6 'plus any changed top-level fields') — omitted entirely when absent, unlike screen_context.v1.json's last_action, which is always present (possibly null) because a full snapshot states its complete state.

last_api.description: Present only when the most recent non-2xx response changed since the base state (docs/07 rule 7, §6).

loading.description: Present only when the loading flag changed since the base state (docs/07 §6).

dirty_fields.description: Present only when the dirty-fields set changed since the base state (docs/07 §6, rule 4).

changed_component.description: A full current component, same field vocabulary as screen_context.v1.json's per-role components, validated here at the common-fields level rather than the full discriminated union (see file description). role is still checked against the closed docs/07 §4 vocabulary.

component_identity.description: Wire-level identity for a removal: role + label (docs/07 §6).

last_action.description: Duplicated locally from screen_context.v1.json — this walker only resolves local $ref (see backend/tests/contract/test_context_protocol.py), and no schema file in this repo cross-references another.

last_api.description: Duplicated locally from screen_context.v1.json, same reason as last_action above.
